requirement.statement: XNL mutation diff SHALL use element #id as the identity key for node alignment and move detection and MUST NOT emit ordinary field updates for #id; strict update mutations SHALL preserve the full-tree identity skeleton and strict structural writes SHALL not overwrite an occupied identified destination.

case.given: Two trees contain the same uniquely identified element under different parents or indexes.
case.when: diffNodes compares the trees in identity mode.
case.then: The mutation set SHALL identify the structural move by that #id rather than treating #id as changed payload.

case.given: A base or candidate tree contains the same effective identity more than once.
case.when: The strict mutation batch API validates the tree.
case.then: The batch SHALL be rejected with a structured duplicate-identity diagnostic before acceptance.

case.given: An element has no effective identity.
case.when: The batch runs with allow-missing or require-elements identity policy.
case.then: Allow-missing SHALL accept the absence while require-elements SHALL reject it with a structured diagnostic.

case.given: A caller submits an add, update, or delete mutation whose target is an element #id field.
case.when: The strict mutation batch API validates the mutation before apply.
case.then: The batch SHALL reject it with IDENTITY_MUTATION_FORBIDDEN, SHALL leave the base unchanged, and identity replacement SHALL only be representable as old-node delete plus new-node add.

case.given: An update mutation replaces a whole node or container and changes, adds, removes, swaps, or relocates an identified descendant.
case.when: The strict mutation batch compares the ordered full-tree identity skeleton before and after that update.
case.then: The batch SHALL reject it with IDENTITY_MUTATION_FORBIDDEN and SHALL expose only an unchanged base clone.

case.given: An element has no explicit #id and an update replaces its metadata container so the effective fallback identity changes or disappears.
case.when: The strict batch compares the full-tree identity skeleton before and after the update.
case.then: The batch SHALL reject it with IDENTITY_MUTATION_FORBIDDEN even though the mutation target container has no identity itself.

case.given: An element has no explicit #id and its metadata id is the effective compatibility identity.
case.when: A strict identity-mode batch directly adds, updates, or deletes that metadata id map key.
case.then: The batch SHALL reject it with IDENTITY_MUTATION_FORBIDDEN; an element with explicit #id SHALL retain the existing identity-mode compatibility behavior for metadata id.

case.given: An element has an explicit #id and also carries compatibility metadata id.
case.when: An ordinary update changes only the metadata fallback while the explicit #id and all structural identity paths remain stable.
case.then: The identity skeleton SHALL continue using #id precedence and SHALL not misclassify the payload update as an identity replacement.

case.given: A whole-node or container update switches an element between explicit #id and metadata fallback while preserving the same identity string.
case.when: The strict batch compares the ordered full-tree identity descriptors before and after the update.
case.then: The batch SHALL reject the raw identity authority transition with IDENTITY_MUTATION_FORBIDDEN; #id SHALL remain an alignment authority rather than ordinary update payload.

case.given: An add or move targets an occupied property, map key, or extend destination whose existing subtree contains an identified element.
case.when: The strict batch validates the assignment-style destination before apply.
case.then: The batch SHALL reject it with IDENTITY_MUTATION_FORBIDDEN rather than silently replacing the existing identity.

case.given: An add inserts at an ordinary array list index or an add/move targets an empty assignment-style destination.
case.when: The strict batch applies the explicit structural mutation.
case.then: The operation SHALL remain eligible for normal identity and result validation.

case.given: Two Extend bodies contain the same children in a different order, with or without effective identities under the selected policy.
case.when: diffNodes compares them and the strict batch applies the produced mutations.
case.then: The diff SHALL express the reorder as explicit same-level identity or pathBefore move mutations, SHALL NOT update extend.order as ordinary payload, and the applied value SHALL equal the target.

case.given: An Extend child keeps its identity while its tag and therefore its keyed storage name change.
case.when: diffNodes constructs and the strict batch applies the retag mutation set.
case.then: The diff SHALL use an explicit move destination key to migrate the children key at the target order index, update the child tag, and leave a coherent Extend body; a standalone tag update without key migration SHALL be rejected with RESULT_STRUCTURE_INVALID.

case.given: An identified Extend child is retagged and moves from a later index to an earlier index or from an earlier index to a later index.
case.when: diffNodes emits and the strict batch applies the mutation set.
case.then: The move destinationKey SHALL carry the new storage key independently from the moved node's old tag, and both direction cases SHALL apply exactly to the target.

case.given: An Extend index add or cross-parent move would write a child tag already occupied by a different identified child.
case.when: The strict batch validates the destination before source extraction or insertion.
case.then: The batch SHALL inspect the children[value.tag] occupant, reject replacement of a different child without overwriting either child, and keep a same-source reorder or delete-then-add replacement eligible regardless of the sibling currently at the target order index.

case.given: A whole-node update preserves every identified descendant at the same relative structural path.
case.when: The strict mutation batch updates tag or ordinary payload.
case.then: The update SHALL remain eligible for normal precondition, apply, and result validation, except that an Extend child retag SHALL also satisfy the structural key migration and final coherence rules.

case.given: A batch deletes the old identified node and adds a new node with a different identity.
case.when: The ordered strict batch applies the explicit structural mutations.
case.then: The replacement SHALL remain eligible for atomic acceptance when all other validation passes.

case.given: Identity-bearing DataElement or TextElement nodes occur in metadata, attributes, body, or extend under allow-missing or require-elements policy.
case.when: TREE_UPDATE, OBJECT_UPDATE, add, delete, or move mutations pass through strict and legacy entries.
case.then: The strict entry SHALL enforce effective-identity continuity and occupied-destination rules while legacy applyMutations SHALL preserve its existing behavior.
